newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH GOVT SAYS APPROVES INCENTIVE PLAN FOR INTEL.
newsitem.headline: CZECH GOVT SAYS APPROVES INCENTIVE PLAN FOR INTEL.

text.p: The Czech government on Wednesday approved a proposal to grant investment incentives to Intel Corp. if it chooses the Czech Republic to build a $300-500 million greenfield computer microchip plant.
"The government approved some investment incentives in the case of Intel," said Industry and Trade Minister Karel Kuhnl speaking after a regular government meeting.

Intel representatives said on Monday the Czech Republic is on a short list of countries which the firm is evaluating as a possible location for the plant. Locations in the Middle East and Asia are also under consideration, Intel said.
Local media have reported that Intel is seeking tax holidays and other incentives, but would generate for the Czech government up to 1revenue over eight years.
The plant is expected to initially employee 3,000 people and could grow to as many as 9,000 at full capacity.
Industrial areas near the Czech cities of Plzen and Pardubice were under consideration, the daily Pravo has reported.
Matsushita has just opened a $66 million Panasonic television plant in the Borska Pole industrial park near Plzen, one of the largest greenfield investment's to date in the Czech Republic.
